intent.text: Demonstrate that mathc validate emits one Warn MC-VERIFIER-SCHEME-UNKNOWN diagnostic per non-canonical verifier scheme token in obligations[*].acceptance.all[*].verifier, while still returning parse-ok on stdout.

commitment: mathc validate returns parse-ok AND emits MC-VERIFIER-SCHEME-UNKNOWN on stderr for every non-canonical scheme token. Severity is Warn, not Block.

outcomes.statement: Three non-canonical scheme tokens produce three Warn MC-VERIFIER-SCHEME-UNKNOWN diagnostics.

assumptions.statement: This fixture carries exactly three non-canonical scheme tokens: 'mathc-foo-impl-runs-on-fixture', 'binary-exists', 'brew-tap-installed'.
assumptions.consequence_if_false: Warning count drifts from the expected 3

obligations.claim: Every non-canonical verifier scheme token surfaces as a Warn diagnostic.
A list mixing canonical and non-canonical schemes surfaces only the non-canonical ones.

counterexample: An unknown-scheme conformance fixture does not carry dialectical content for the kernel-checked rule; the kernel requires counterexample + antithesis for mode >= standard regardless of fixture intent, so this fixture carries documentary content naming the strongest objection considered and rejected.
antithesis: This conformance fixture asserts three MC-VERIFIER-SCHEME-UNKNOWN diagnostics fire on this file (one per non-canonical token, two obligation paths, four total tokens with three unknown). The v3 dialectic antithesis slot is unrelated to that assertion; the author considered and rejected the counter-position that an unknown-scheme demo need not carry dialectic content because its purpose is a validator diagnostic, not a dialectic test. The kernel requires antithesis for mode >= standard regardless of fixture intent, so the fixture carries a documentary antithesis string naming the position considered and rejected.
